doc.title: Carmen Caramanica interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, July 27, 2011

title: Advising students who want to be professional musicians
summary: He tells them to try music school, find their level and network, and learns technology from students.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Nice. So let’s say I had a son and I sent him to you and he really wanted to be a professional musician, but his talent level was medium. Do you have those kind of situations?
And how have you learned to — what have you learned to say?

Okay. If they’re at a point where they have to decide what they want to do after high school, I get a lot of that. I say okay, apply to some colleges, get your audition material ready, see if you get in. If you get in the school, okay, and if you’re going to go for a performance degree or a music ed degree or whatever it is, try it for a semester or two semesters. If you’re not sure or if you can’t get into something on a higher level, go to OCC if they’ll still let you in, or some of the community colleges that have got a basic music program, and see how you like it. You’re going to find out an awful lot about how well you do compared to the guy sitting next to you. Sometimes — there is a place in Los Angeles called MIT, Musician’s Institute of Technology. It used to be GIT, Guitar Institute of Technology. And they have a degree program now, but originally it was a one-year inclusive program of just playing, lessons, recording sessions, going on a short tour with some of the bands, learning what it’s like to really be in the business. And some of my students went and came back after completing the course, and said “you know I really figured that I can’t do this thing professionally. These guys are too good. I don’t © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -18-

stand a chance. They’re just incredibly excellent.” I know there are people that have gone that still maintained their music thing but they realized if I’m going to be trying to get these jobs like the guys in Los Angeles or New York, if they’re that good, the other half is you don’t know the right people, because a lot of it is a very closed society. These kids grew up with each other. Kids that went to Hollywood High School and their fathers are producers. They’re going to get the gigs. So anyway basically I tell them if you’re interested in becoming a musician you’ve got to go to school. You’ve got to go to a music school where other people are interested in the same thing as you are. You network that way. You find out how good you are and how good you’re not. And you kind of let the world show them what they need to do rather than have me try to tell them.
That sounds like good advice. Let them find out on their own. And then they won’t hold it against their parents too if Mom and Dad say you know what, you really need to go into geology.

And of course they can’t blame you as a teacher either, well you told me I was good enough or you told me I wasn’t good enough. No I say hey, go try it. If you can do it, you’ll know. If you can’t well — I used to take the approach where I’d try to talk them out of it because I’d say “you don’t know how hard it is out there, you don’t want to do this.” And if I could talk them out of it, and they say well I’ve decided to do something else, then I’d say well I’m glad you did because if I can talk you out of it you don’t stand a chance anyway. So I used to try that approach. But now I think I’ve found the other way. Encourage them but it doesn’t take long — if they can make it past the first year in school there’s a good chance they’ll stay. And if they don’t —
Do you encourage them to develop other skills besides just being a player?

Yeah. And it’s so easy because I learn a lot about what I know now about musical technology from these kids. No they help me. If I’m trying to do something “oh Mr. Caramanica do this.” “Oh thank you, I didn’t know.” Yeah. So there is no problem saying you should get this program or that program or let’s work with this thing, they just take right to it.
